catalog_quote: The placement of word stress is not predictable and needs to be remembered for all stems with more than one syllable. For words in isolation it is indicated in the phonemic transcription with an acute above the nucleus vowel of the stressed syllable (´). The acute is omitted on monosyllabic stressed stems in isolation. Stress can be contrastive, but full minimal pairs are rare and usually not valid for more than one dialect. ... Although the position of word stress is not generally predictable, there is a tendency for it to fall on the final stem syllable of a word (before any suffixes, inflectional elements or clitics). ... It is not impossible for lexical stress to fall on a suffix. Stress remains in the same position throughout inflectional paradigms, so that if lexical stress is on the suffix, the suffix will be stressed in all inflectional forms, e.g. mus-é (DIR), mus-ḗ (OBL) 'mous…

audit.reasoning: The coding 'lexical' (unpredictable, stored per stem, contrastive, with a stem-final tendency and paradigm-stable position, no tone) rests on a 2024 684-page reference grammar (Cologne PhD, open access at KUPS) which we hold as PDF+text; every sentence of the deciding quotation, the domain quotation and the srule's retraction claim was found verbatim at the stated sections/pages (2.1.4.1-2.1.4.1.2 pp. 106-108, 2.1.5.1 p. 110). Halfmann is Glottolog's top grammar for the languoid and explicitly reviews all earlier stress remarks (Grjunberg 1980, Fussman 1983, Strand, Yoshioka 2021); No instrumental study

sources.citation: Strand, Richard F. 1997b (last edited 2011). The Sound System of kâmvʹiri. nuristan.info/Nuristani/Kamkata/Kom/KomLanguage/Lexicon/
sources.quote: 'Three accentual symbols occur before an accented word to denote the position of accent as follows: ` = accent on first syllable, ^ = accent on second syllable, ´ = accent on final syllable (of a word-stem). The latter accent occurs only with polysyllabic words of foreign origin, following the Persian accentual pattern. Alternatively, accent is indicated by an accent mark ( ʹ ) before the accented vowel.' sources.citation: Yoshioka, Noboru. 2021. Nominal echo formations in Kati in the context of languages of northern Pakistan. Bulletin of the National Museum of Ethnology 45(3): 429-440. doi:10.15021/00009640
sources.quote: 'An acute accent symbol (ˊ) over vowels denotes a (possibly indistinctive) high pitch accent in multisyllabic words, while I omit its use for monosyllabic words because the only vowels of the words must take a high pitch accent.' A tentative transcription note only (the 'high pitch accent' Halfmann p.106 cites and rejects in favour of stress accent); says nothing about predictability of position.
